extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy, legislators, jurists, and historians of law and government
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative principles about the distribution of powers, judicial procedure, provincial administration, slavery, and the relation of laws to national character from a classical political-theory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public spectacles as political catalysts
rubrics_metrics.description: Le spectacle de la mort de Virginie... fit chasser les décemvirs; la robe sanglante de César remit Rome dans la servitude. (Public spectacles — shocking public events — move popular sentiment and precipitate constitutional change.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical examples (Lucrèce, the mutilated debtor, Virginie, Caesar's bloody robe) to evaluate how visible events accelerate political mobilization. Anti-pattern: ignoring the emotive power of public displays when diagnosing causes of regime change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation and limitation of popular legislative power
rubrics_metrics.description: La puissance législative du peuple doit être réglée et bornée — ex. les censeurs et consuls formaient le corps du peuple et limitaient la puissance du peuple législatif; sans bornes, le peuple peut exercer une puissance 'exorbitante'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether popular legislative organs are constrained by institutions (censors, consuls, senate) that periodically reconstitute or check the popular body. Example: Tiberius Gracchus transferring affranchis into city tribes; anti-pattern: unregulated popular legislative monopolies that override other constitutional organs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance among legislative, executive, and judicial powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Il faut qu'il y ait balance entre les trois pouvoirs; la liberté dépend de la distribution de ces pouvoirs entre peuple, sénat et magistrats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate constitutional designs by whether each major power is distributed so as to counterbalance the others (e.g., people holding legislative power, senate holding parts of executive/judicial powers). Anti-pattern: removal of one organ's share (e.g., judges moved from senate to equestrians) that breaks constitutional equilibrium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentration of powers in few magistrates
rubrics_metrics.description: Dix hommes (décemvirs) eurent seuls toute la puissance législative, exécutrice et judiciaire — résultat: tyrannie cruelle; similarly, proconsuls in provinces with all three powers become despotic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat concentration of multiple powers in a single body or individual as a red flag for tyranny; prefer institutional separations. Example: the decemvirs' usurpation and provincial 'pachas' (proconsuls) who exercised all three powers. Scoring note: the more powers concentrated, the worse for liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial, temporary, and case-specific judicial appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Le préteur formait chaque année une liste et prenait les juges du consentement des parties; on tirait au sort les juges pour chaque affaire — cela favorisait la liberté.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate judicial selection by temporariness, rotation, party consent, and lot-drawing per case. Positive features: annual praetors, judges chosen per case, consent of parties. Anti-patterns: lifetime judge appointments dominated by a private economic order that undermines impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of fact-finding and questions of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Les juges ne décidaient que des questions de fait; les questions de droit étaient portées au tribunal des centumvirs — distinction fact vs law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a system separates factual determinations from complex legal questions (dedicated legal tribunals for law; juries/lay judges for facts). Anti-pattern: conflating fact and complex legal reasoning in bodies ill-equipped for the latter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction allocated by gravity of penalty (Twelve Tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: La loi des Douze Tables ordonna qu'on ne pourrait décider de la vie d'un citoyen que dans les grands états du peuple; le peuple (comices par tribus) ne jugea plus que les crimes dont la peine n'était qu'une amende.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether jurisdictional rules assign cases by seriousness (capital vs pecuniary penalties) to avoid overlap and to force consultation among bodies. Positive outcome: conciliation between plebeians and senate. Anti-pattern: unclear jurisdiction allowing conflicts between bodies over severe punishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate's control as check on popular and executive excesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Le sénat disposait des deniers publics, arbitrant des affaires des alliés, décidant de la guerre et de la paix, distribuant provinces, nommant et jugeant rois — une institution qui contrebalance le peuple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a council or assembly has financial, foreign-policy, and administrative roles that can constrain transient popular impulses or executive adventurism. Anti-pattern: a powerless senate that cannot check other organs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen selection power coupled with professional administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Le peuple réservait surtout le droit d'élire les magistrats et de confirmer les actes; mais la direction des grandes affaires demanda au sénat la sagesse consommée nécessaire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance popular electoral authority with experienced administrative bodies for execution. Positive design: elections plus confirmation mechanisms. Anti-pattern: leaving all executive functions to inexperienced popular bodies without institutional expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provincial governance must avoid granting governors unilateral powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Dans les provinces, les préteurs et proconsuls avaient la puissance législative, exécutrice et de juger — entraînant tyrannie aux extrémités; la liberté au centre, tyrannie aux extrémités.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate imperial/provincial administration by whether governors hold combined unchecked powers; prefer institutional arrangements that split legislative, executive, and judicial authority in provinces. Anti-pattern: 'pachas de la république' — remote magistrates with despotic authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation fairness tied to constitutional representation (Servius Tullius principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Servius Tullius distribua les citoyens en six classes selon leurs richesses et fixa la part de l'impôt à proportion de celle que chacun avait dans le gouvernement — garantie d'équité fiscale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tax systems for proportionality linked to political representation or stake in government. Positive sign: taxation rules embedded in constitutional class structure. Anti-pattern: arbitrary exactions in provinces while citizens at center pay equitably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial competence and social class of judges affects liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: Transférer les jugements aux chevaliers (ordre des traitants) affaiblit la constitution; les juges pris parmi les sénateurs formaient un contrepoids au peuple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess who composes tribunals: moving judicial power to economically self-interested classes (e.g., contractors/publicans) undermines public justice. Anti-pattern: judges beholden to commercial interests leading to corruption and breakdown of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slavery lacks moral or legal justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Les trois raisons jurisconsultes (captifs de guerre, vente par débiteurs, naissance) ne sont point sensées; l'esclavage n'est ni bon par nature ni utile au maître ou à l'esclave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject canonical justifications for slavery: war capture does not justify lifelong enslavement; voluntary sale of liberty is incoherent; descent-based slavery is indefensible. Examples: critique of jurisconsultes' threefold origin. Use these rebuttals when evaluating laws permitting slavery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural, religious, or 'civilizational' difference is not a ground for enslavement
rubrics_metrics.description: L'opinion que la religion ou la différence des coutumes donne un droit de réduire en servitude est critiquée — ex. justification used by Spaniards regarding Americans and by Europeans regarding Africans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating laws/practices, treat appeals to cultural inferiority or religious difference as illegitimate bases for enslavement or domination. Anti-pattern: legitimizing conquest/exploitation by citing dietary, grooming, or religious differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislation must respect and follow the 'spirit' of the nation
rubrics_metrics.description: Il faut que le législateur suive l'esprit de la nation lorsqu'il n'est pas contraire aux principes du gouvernement; les meilleures lois exigent que les esprits soient préparés.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess proposed legal reforms for consonance with national character (climate, religion, laws, moeurs, manières) and for whether the populace is culturally prepared; radical imposition contrary to spirit produces resistance. Examples: Varus' tribunal before the Germans, difficulties imposing Roman formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid laws that attempt to erase valuable national manners or virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Qu'on ne cherche pas à gêner les manières naturelles d'une nation sous peine d'ôter ses vertus; 'Ne pas tout corriger' — conserver la vivacité et la gaieté qui peuvent être sources de richesse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reformist legislation for potential collateral loss of beneficial customs (commerce, arts, sociability). Anti-pattern: pedantic laws that remove a nation's productive or civil virtues under the pretext of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish two kinds of tyranny: real and of opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: La tyrannie réelle consiste dans la violence du gouvernement; la tyrannie d'opinion survient lorsque les gouvernants établissent des choses qui choquent la manière de penser d'une nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging governments/laws, consider both physical repression and legal/cultural measures that alienate the populace. Remedy differs: repressing physical tyranny vs aligning law with national sentiment to avoid opinion-tyranny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harness vanity/productive pride, guard against destructive national pride
rubrics_metrics.description: La vanité encourage luxe, industrie, arts et commerce; l'orgueil (pride) conduit à paresse, pauvreté et destruction des nations conquis par eux.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cultural policies by whether they promote productive vanity (stimulating arts and commerce) while discouraging corrosive national pride that fosters complacency and decline.
